chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Salih al-Lafa'ifi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — spread the earth from beneath the Kaaba to Mina, then spread it from Mina to Arafat, then spread it from Arafat to Mina. So the earth originates from Arafat, and Arafat from Mina, and Mina from the Kaaba.

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Kaaba — sacred cube-shaped structure in Mecca, the axis of creation
key_terms.دَحَا: Spread, evened out, extended (the earth) — an act of divine creation
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat — the plain where pilgrims gather on the 9th of Dhu al-Hijja, the culminating rite of Hajj
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina — a valley near Mecca, a central site of the Hajj

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about how God spread the earth from the Kaaba?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the cosmological origin and sacred geography of the Hijaz: the earth was spread outward in successive stages from beneath the Kaaba — first to Mina, then to Arafat, then back to Mina — establishing the Kaaba as the primordial center of creation. This hadith grounds the sacred rites of Hajj in the very act of creation, explaining why each location visited during pilgrimage possesses a special sanctity rooted in the origin of the earth itself.
